idiom_name: renderer registry plus one negotiation point over a shared projection
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep the model presentation-free, derive a projection or logical view that all representations share, represent each view technology as its own renderer over that projection, register the renderers in one table keyed by representation (media type or channel), and centralise the choice in a single negotiation point that reads the request (Accept header, format suffix, channel) and dispatches to the table. Keep change notification out of the request/response case - views are produced on demand - and introduce an observer or listener list only when several views stay alive at the same time; never let a renderer fetch from the store itself, it receives the same projection object as its siblings.
code_sketch:
model      = load(id)                     # one model, presentation-free
projection = present(model)               # shared logical view: selection + formatting
view       = registry.match(requested)    # negotiation: media type / channel -> renderer
response   = view.render(projection)      # one technology per view
# live variant: model.on_change([table.render, chart.render, inspector.render])
pitfalls: Letting each view load or filter the data on its own recreates the duplication the pattern removes, together with the drift.
Deciding the representation in several places (path suffix in one route, Accept header in another, a flag in a third) makes behaviour unpredictable; keep one negotiation point.
No defined unsupported-representation path: answer a request no view matches with 406 and an explanation instead of silently serving the default representation.

Wrong move: Return the persistence entity directly to every renderer -> this fails because serializers expose internal fields or relations and can trigger inconsistent lazy loading -> instead project the model once and give each view representation-safe data.

Wrong move: Let renderer order, URL suffixes, and Accept headers choose independently -> this fails because clients and caches can receive different representations or silent fallbacks -> instead centralize negotiation, document precedence, and return 406 when no renderer matches.

Wrong move: Add a new view by copying queries and business rules -> this fails because filtering, rounding, and authorization drift across representations -> instead reuse one model or projection and keep only format-specific rendering in the new view.
